medications.dose: 2.5 mg once daily (titrate to 5 mg after 2–4 weeks if tolerated, up to 10 mg max)
medications.purpose: Lower clinic blood pressure to <140/90 mmHg (stage 2 hypertension) and provide cardioprotective effect
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 first‑line treatment for patients <55 y without Afro‑Caribbean ethnicity – ACE‑I recommended (see first_line_treatment)

assumptions_warnings: NICE NG136 requires baseline renal function (eGFR) and serum potassium before starting an ACE‑I – not available, assumed eGFR ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m² and K⁺ normal.
QRISK cardiovascular risk assessment is required for statin decision‑making – lipid profile and other risk factors missing.
Liver function tests not recorded – assumed normal for ACE‑I safety.
Blood pressure measurement method not specified – assume clinic measurement; ambulatory monitoring may be needed.
No documented drug allergies – assume none.
treatment_summary: Initiate ramipril 2.5 mg daily as first‑line therapy for essential hypertension per NICE NG136, with titration to target dose based on BP response and renal/electrolyte monitoring. Arrange baseline labs (eGFR, creatinine, potassium, lipids, glucose) and calculate QRISK. Provide lifestyle advice (salt <6 g/day, DASH diet, 150 min/week exercise, weight loss, limit alcohol, smoking cessation). Review BP and labs in 2–4 weeks, then continue lifelong with annual review.
